title: Berkeley and Oakland Rent Increases for 2027 Explained (Video)

findings.quote: So a tenant who moved in any time in 2025 gets their first increase on January 1, 2027.
findings.root_cause: The script makes eligibility sound automatic and applies Berkeley's fully-covered-unit rule to all Berkeley rentals. The page's introduction and takeaways repeat the broad claim; lease and compliance conditions are omitted. Source: https://rentboard.berkeleyca.gov/rights-responsibilities/rent-levels/annual-general-adjustment
findings.fix: Replace with: 'For fully rent-controlled Berkeley units, 2025 move-ins first become AGA-eligible on January 1, 2027; 2026 move-ins first become eligible in January 2028, subject to the lease, proper notice and Rent Board compliance.' Use the same qualifications in the introduction, takeaways and parent script.
findings.future_prevention: Recheck page prose, takeaways and script together whenever the parent changes.

findings.quote: Units covered only by state law can go up as much as eight point eight percent.
findings.root_cause: The script does not state the August 2026-July 2027 window for this rate or its rolling-period limit; it can sound like a fresh increase allowance at each anniversary. The page should not imply every state-only unit can take the full amount regardless of earlier increases.
findings.fix: Replace with: 'For AB 1482-only units, the cap for increases effective August 1, 2026 through July 31, 2027 is 8.8% over a rolling 12 months, not an additional 8.8% after an earlier increase.' Use the same date window in Key Takeaways. The official Oakland allowable-increases page corroborates 8.8%; the DRE 2026 guide corroborates the rolling-period framework.
findings.future_prevention: Include the effective window and rolling-period basis in every standalone rate summary.

findings.quote: For a January 1 increase, mail the thirty-day notice by November 25, or deliver it in person by December 1.
findings.root_cause: This standalone instruction omits when 30 days is enough and assumes within-California mailing. The targets provide adequate buffer for that scenario; the error is their universal framing. Official DRE 2026 guide, printed pp.44-46: https://www.dre.ca.gov/publications/ResourceGuidebook/2026_Landlord_Tenant_Guide.pdf
findings.fix: Replace with: 'For a lawful January 1 increase that qualifies for 30-day notice, our conservative targets are November 25 for first-class mailing within California, or December 1 for personal delivery. Larger cumulative increases or mailing from elsewhere need a different notice calculation.' Repeat this qualification in the takeaways and cite the DRE guide in Resources.
findings.future_prevention: Carry the notice scenario's conditions into short-form scripts.

findings.quote: That's why, at AEBP, Berkeley is the one city where we raise rent on January 1.
findings.root_cause: The cited company records support the portfolio count, but not the new January 1 and anniversary policies or unit-level tracking practices. No relevant confirmation appeared in the anecdote log.
findings.fix: Retain only after Brian confirms the practice in an identifiable internal record. Pending confirmation, replace with: 'For eligible fully covered Berkeley units, January 1 can avoid waiting until a later lease anniversary.' Replace 'Outside Berkeley, we time increases to each unit’s lease anniversary' with 'Outside Berkeley, check the lease and the local eligibility rules before choosing an increase date.' Remove unconfirmed tracking claims from the CTA; retain the documented 600+ unit count.
findings.future_prevention: Use documented operational facts or clearly framed professional analysis.
